senses.definition: present participle and gerund of knit
The action of the verb to knit; the process of producing knitted material.
Material that has been, or is being knitted.
examples: She put down her knitting and went to answer the phone.

quotes.text: At Kiwi, 40 miles from Nelson [New Zealand], eight women installed themselves in the goods shed, taking with them their knitting, and a supply of food and magazines. The demolition crew was unable to pull the building down without injuring them.
quotes.reference: 1955 December, “Notes and News: Women Delay Railway Demolition”, in Railway Magazine, page 878:

quotes.text: My suggestion would be to electrify the uphill bits only, in each direction, and to use diesel traction when coming down the other side. Massive savings on posts and knitting for a start.
